problem_statement:
Fancy Binary Search
fancy-binsearch


Input:
    arr: A sorted list of ints
    x: A value to find

Output:
    The lowest index i such that arr[i] == x, or -1 if x not in arr

Example:
    >>> find_first_in_sorted([3, 4, 5, 5, 5, 5, 6], 5)
    2

bugs.description: The binary-search loop uses `lo <= hi` even though `hi` is an exclusive upper bound initialized to `len(arr)`. This permits an iteration with `lo == hi == len(arr)`, causing `arr[mid]` to access past the end of the list.
bugs.fix: Use `while lo < hi:` so midpoint indexing only occurs while the exclusive search interval is nonempty.

bugs.description: When x is greater than arr[mid], the recursive search keeps mid in the interval by calling binsearch(mid, end). If mid is the lower bound, this can repeat the same interval indefinitely instead of making progress.
bugs.fix: Exclude the already-tested midpoint from the right half by recursing with binsearch(mid + 1, end).

bugs.description: The recursive Euclidean algorithm call passes the arguments in the wrong order. It recurses with `(a % b, b)`, which may fail to reduce the second argument and can loop indefinitely (for example, `gcd(35, 21)`).
bugs.fix: Recurse as `gcd(b, a % b)` so the remainder becomes the second argument and the algorithm progresses toward the `b == 0` base case.
